title: Louis's and Duke's itineraries and Glaser's favoritism
summary: Willard compares Armstrong's lighter itineraries with Ellington's; Duke complained Glaser gave Louis better dates.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, I remember seeing Louis' itinerary the same time I looked at Duke's itinerary and (inaudible) out of ABC (inaudible). Louis has always looked a little more considerate, like somebody who cared about his health and his strength, that there would be a day off once in a while, and there wouldn't be as long jumps to do. Duke used to have the most absurd itinerary. He'd go 1,000 miles, and then he'd back up 500, and then he'd go 1,000 again.
We used to do it. But when Louis started getting sick, then he started lightening up on them. We used to do the same thing.
And then Duke used to say, Joe Glaser doesn't care as much about me as he does Louis. He gives Louis better dates.
